summary: This mishnah tells us until what time we may daven each tefillah: Shacharis, Mincha, Maariv, and Musaf.
stIntro: This mishna determines the times beyond which the different prayers may not be recited. According to the Rabbis,

chunks.en: The morning tefillah, Shacharis, may be said until midday.
chunks.st: the morning prayer may be recited until noon.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

words.note: Rabbi Yehuda was a great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: until four hours into the day.
chunks.st: It may be recited only until four hours after sunrise.

words.note: Hours counted from sunrise, about a third of the day.

chunks.en: The tefillah of Mincha may be said until evening.
chunks.st: According to the Rabbis, the afternoon prayer may be recited until the evening.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

words.note: Rabbi Yehuda was a great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: until plag haMincha, the middle of the late afternoon.
chunks.explain: About an hour and a quarter before night.
chunks.st: It may be recited only until the midpoint of the afternoon [pelag haminḥa],
chunks.stMore: i.e., the midpoint of the period that begins with the sacrifice of the daily afternoon offering and ends at nightfall, which is the end of the afternoon.
chunks.basisNote: The time amount is from Bartenura.

words.note: Plag haMincha, a little over an hour before nightfall.

chunks.en: The evening tefillah, Maariv, has no set time; it may be said all night.
chunks.st: The evening prayer may be recited throughout the night and is not fixed to a specific hour.
chunks.basisNote: Bartenura adds: the wording hints Maariv was once optional; today it is a must.

chunks.en: And Musaf may be said all day.
chunks.st: According to the Rabbis, the additional prayer may be recited all day.

words.note: The extra tefillah on Shabbos, Yom Tov, and Rosh Chodesh.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

words.note: Rabbi Yehuda was a great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: until seven hours into the day.
chunks.st: It may be recited only until seven hours after sunrise.

summary: Rabbi Nechunya ben Hakanah said a short tefillah when he went into the beis midrash and when he left. Going in, he asked not to make any mistakes, and going out, he thanked Hashem for his share in learning.
stIntro: In addition to the halakhot relating to the fixed prayers, the Gemara relates:

chunks.he: רַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא בֶּן הַקָּנָה הָיָה מִתְפַּלֵּל
chunks.en: Rabbi Nechunya ben Hakanah used to daven
chunks.st: Rabbi Neḥunya ben Hakana would recite

words.note: Rabbi Nechunya ben Hakanah was a great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.he: בִּכְנִיסָתוֹ לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ וּבִיצִיאָתוֹ תְּפִלָּה קְצָרָה.
chunks.en: a short tefillah when he went into the beis midrash and when he left it.
chunks.st: a brief prayer upon his entrance into the study hall and upon his exit.

words.note: The beis midrash, where people learn Torah.

chunks.en: They asked him,
chunks.st: They said to him:

chunks.en: what is this tefillah for?
chunks.st: The study hall is not a dangerous place that would warrant a prayer when entering and exiting, so what room is there for this prayer?

chunks.en: He told them,
chunks.st: He said to them:

chunks.en: When I go in, I daven
chunks.st: Upon my entrance, I pray

chunks.en: that nothing should go wrong because of me,
chunks.explain: Like making a mistake in a halacha.
chunks.st: that no mishap will transpire caused by me in the study hall.

chunks.he: וּבִיצִיאָתִי אֲנִי נוֹתֵן הוֹדָיָה עַל חֶלְקִי:
chunks.en: and when I go out, I thank Hashem for my share.
chunks.explain: That he gets to sit and learn Torah.
chunks.st: And upon my exit, I give thanks for my portion.

summary: Rabban Gamliel says we must say all of Shemoneh Esrei every day. Rabbi Yehoshua says a short version is enough, and Rabbi Akiva says it depends on whether the person knows it well.
stIntro: The mishna cites a dispute with regard to the obligation to recite the Amida prayer, also known as Shemoneh Esreh, the prayer of eighteen blessings, or simply as tefilla, prayer.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel says:

words.note: Rabban Gamliel was the leader of the Jewish people in the time of the Mishnah.

chunks.he: בְּכָל יוֹם מִתְפַּלֵּל אָדָם שְׁמֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה.
chunks.en: every day a person davens Shemoneh Esrei.
chunks.st: Each and every day a person recites the prayer of eighteen blessings.

words.note: Shemoneh Esrei, the tefillah of eighteen brachos.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua says:

words.note: Rabbi Yehoshua was a great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: a short version of Shemoneh Esrei.
chunks.st: A short prayer is sufficient, and one only recites an abridged version of the prayer of eighteen blessings.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says an intermediate opinion:

words.note: Rabbi Akiva was a great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: if he knows his tefillah smoothly by heart,
chunks.st: If he is fluent in his prayer,

chunks.en: he should daven all of Shemoneh Esrei.
chunks.st: he recites the prayer of eighteen blessings,

chunks.en: And if not,
chunks.st: and if not,

chunks.en: a short version of Shemoneh Esrei.
chunks.st: he need only recite an abridged version of the prayer of eighteen blessings.

summary: Rabbi Eliezer teaches that davening must not be like a chore, but should be asking Hashem from the heart. Rabbi Yehoshua gives a short tefillah for someone traveling in a dangerous place.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

words.note: Rabbi Eliezer was a great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: someone who makes his davening like a fixed chore,
chunks.st: One whose prayer is fixed,
chunks.basisNote: "Like a chore" is Bartenura's explanation; Steinsaltz just says "fixed."

chunks.en: his davening is not a real request for mercy.
chunks.st: his prayer is not supplication and is flawed.
chunks.stMore: The Gemara will clarify the halakhic implications of this flaw.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua says:

words.note: Rabbi Yehoshua was a great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: someone who is walking in a dangerous place
chunks.st: One who cannot recite a complete prayer because he is walking in a place of danger,

chunks.en: says a short tefillah.
chunks.st: recites a brief prayer

chunks.en: He says: Hashem, save Your people,
chunks.st: and says: Redeem, Lord, Your people,

chunks.en: the ones left of the Jewish people.
chunks.st: the remnant of Israel,

chunks.he: בְּכָל פָּרָשַׁת הָעִבּוּר יִהְיוּ צָרְכֵיהֶם לְפָנֶיךָ.
chunks.en: At every time of change, may their needs be before You.
chunks.explain: Bartenura says it means: even when they sin.
chunks.st: at every transition [parashat ha’ibur], the meaning of which will be discussed in the Gemara. May their needs be before You.
chunks.basisNote: Steinsaltz leaves the meaning to the Gemara; Bartenura: when they stray into sin.

words.note: Steinsaltz: "every transition." Bartenura: when they stray into sin.

chunks.en: Blessed are You, Hashem, Who hears tefillah.
chunks.st: Blessed are You, Lord, Who listens to prayer.

summary: When we daven, we face toward the Beis HaMikdash. Someone riding a donkey should get off; if he can't, he turns his face, and if he can't do that, he thinks about the Kodesh HaKodashim.
stIntro: While praying, one must face toward the direction of the Holy Temple.

chunks.en: If he was riding on a donkey,
chunks.st: One who was riding on a donkey

chunks.en: he should get off to daven.
chunks.st: should dismount and pray calmly.

chunks.en: And if he cannot get off,
chunks.st: If he is unable to dismount,

chunks.en: he should turn his face toward the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: he should turn his face toward the direction of the Temple.

chunks.he: וְאִם אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְהַחֲזִיר אֶת פָּנָיו,
chunks.en: and if he cannot turn his face,
chunks.st: If he is unable to turn his face,

chunks.en: he should point his heart
chunks.st: it is sufficient that he focus his heart

chunks.en: toward the Kodesh HaKodashim.
chunks.st: opposite the Holy of Holies.

words.note: The Kodesh HaKodashim, the holiest room in the Beis HaMikdash.

summary: Someone traveling on a boat, wagon, or raft who can't turn to face Yerushalayim should think about the Kodesh HaKodashim while he davens.

chunks.en: If he was traveling in a boat
chunks.st: Similarly, one who was traveling in a ship

chunks.en: or in a wagon or on a raft,
chunks.explain: And he cannot turn to face Yerushalayim.
chunks.st: or on a wagon or on a raft [asda] and is unable to turn and face in the direction of Jerusalem,

chunks.en: he should point his heart
chunks.st: should focus his heart

chunks.en: toward the Kodesh HaKodashim.
chunks.st: opposite the Holy of Holies.

words.note: The Kodesh HaKodashim, the holiest room in the Beis HaMikdash.

summary: Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah says Musaf is said only with a community minyan. The Chachamim say it is said with or without one.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:

words.note: Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah was a great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.he: אֵין תְּפִלַּת הַמּוּסָפִין אֶלָּא בְּחֶבֶר עִיר.
chunks.en: Musaf is said only in a town with a minyan.
chunks.st: The additional prayer is only recited in a city where there is a quorum of ten [ḥever ir].
chunks.basisNote: Bartenura: only with a group, not alone.

words.note: The extra tefillah on Shabbos, Yom Tov, and Rosh Chodesh.
A town with a minyan of ten.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: The Rabbis say:

chunks.en: with a town minyan or without one.
chunks.st: One may recite the additional prayer with a ḥever ir or without a ḥever ir.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says in his name,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says another opinion in his name, the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya:

words.note: Rabbi Yehuda was a great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: any place where there is a town minyan,
chunks.st: Any place where there is a ḥever ir,

words.note: A town's group of ten men.

chunks.en: a person davening alone does not have to say Musaf.
chunks.explain: The chazzan's Musaf counts for him.
chunks.st: an individual is completely exempt from reciting the additional prayer.
